question: True or false: for plasma transfusions, group AB is the universal donor?
answer: True. Red cells carry the A and B antigens, so group O cells suit anyone; plasma carries the antibodies, and only AB plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B. So AB plasma can go to any patient, while O plasma, full of both, suits only group O. Just 3 to 4% of people are AB.
move: When the thing being given changes, check whether the rule flips.
trap: Carrying over the red-cell rule that makes O the universal donor.
reference: Klein & Anstee, Mollison's Blood Transfusion in Clinical Medicine, 12th edition, Wiley-Blackwell, 2014
